cases.sentence: В приемной никого уже не было, кроме князя Василия и ___, которые, сидя под портретом Екатерины, о чем-то оживленно говорили.
cases.explain: «старшей княжны» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: There was now no one in the reception room except Prince Vasíli and the eldest princess, who were sitting under the portrait of Catherine the Great and talking eagerly. As soon as they saw Pierre and his companion they became silent, and Pierre thought he saw the princess hide something as she whispered:

cases.sentence: — Но, ___, — кротко и убедительно говорила Анна Михайловна, заступая дорогу от спальни и не пуская княжну, — не будет ли это слишком тяжело для бедного дядюшки в такие минуты, когда ему нужен отдых?
cases.explain: «милая княжна» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “But, my dear princess,” answered Anna Mikháylovna blandly but impressively, blocking the way to the bedroom and preventing the other from passing, “won’t this be too much for poor Uncle at a moment when he needs repose? Worldly conversation at a moment when his soul is already prepared …”

cases.sentence: Князь Василий сидел на кресле, в своей ___, высоко заложив ногу на ногу.
cases.explain: «фамильярной позе» — after the preposition «в», for location or topic.
cases.translation: Prince Vasíli was seated in an easy chair in his familiar attitude, with one leg crossed high above the other. His cheeks, which were so flabby that they looked heavier below, were twitching violently; but he wore the air of a man little concerned in what the two ladies were saying.

cases.sentence: — Я и не знаю, чтó в этой бумаге, — говорила княжна, обращаясь к князю Василью и указывая на ___, который она держала в руках.
cases.explain: «мозаиковый портфель» — after the preposition «на», the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: “I don’t even know what is in this paper,” said the younger of the two ladies, addressing Prince Vasíli and pointing to an inlaid portfolio she held in her hand. “All I know is that his real will is in his writing table, and this is a paper he has forgotten. …”

cases.sentence: — Я знаю только, что ___ у него в бюро, а это забытая бумага...
cases.explain: «настоящее завещание» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “I don’t even know what is in this paper,” said the younger of the two ladies, addressing Prince Vasíli and pointing to an inlaid portfolio she held in her hand. “All I know is that his real will is in his writing table, and this is a paper he has forgotten. …”

cases.sentence: — Я знаю, милая, ___, — сказала Анна Михайловна, хватаясь рукой за портфель и так крепко, что видно было, она не скоро его пустит.
cases.explain: «добрая княжна» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “I know, my dear, kind princess,” said Anna Mikháylovna, seizing the portfolio so firmly that it was plain she would not let go easily. “Dear princess, I beg and implore you, have some pity on him! Je vous en conjure …”

cases.sentence: Я думаю, что он не лишний в ___: не правда ли, князь?
cases.explain: «родственном совете» — after the preposition «в», for location or topic.
cases.translation: “Pierre, my dear, come here. I think he will not be out of place in a family consultation; is it not so, Prince?”

cases.sentence: — Mais, mon prince,[205] Но, князь, говорила Анна Михайловна, — после такого ___ дайте ему минуту покоя.
cases.explain: «великого таинства» — after the preposition «после», the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: “But, Prince,” said Anna Mikháylovna, “after such a solemn sacrament, allow him a moment’s peace! Here, Pierre, tell them your opinion,” said she, turning to the young man who, having come quite close, was gazing with astonishment at the angry face of the princess which had lost all dignity, and at the twitching cheeks of Prince Vasíli.

cases.sentence: Вот, Пьер, скажите ваше мнение, — обратилась она к ___, который, вплоть подойдя к ним, удивленно смотрел на озлобленное, потерявшее всё приличие лицо княжны и на перепрыгивающие щеки князя Василия.
cases.explain: «молодому человеку» — after the preposition «к», the dative marks the indirect object or recipient.
cases.translation: “But, Prince,” said Anna Mikháylovna, “after such a solemn sacrament, allow him a moment’s peace! Here, Pierre, tell them your opinion,” said she, turning to the young man who, having come quite close, was gazing with astonishment at the angry face of the princess which had lost all dignity, and at the twitching cheeks of Prince Vasíli.

cases.sentence: Пьер заметил, что он был бледен и что нижняя челюсть его прыгала и тряслась, как в ___.
cases.explain: «лихорадочной дрожи» — after the preposition «в», for location or topic.
cases.translation: Prince Vasíli came next. He staggered to the sofa on which Pierre was sitting and dropped onto it, covering his face with his hand. Pierre noticed that he was pale and that his jaw quivered and shook as if in an ague.
